paper_metadata.title: A Method for Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph Dynamic Construction
paper_metadata.venue: 2022 5th International Conference on Big Data Technologies (ICBDT 2022)
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper proposes a dynamically growing Traditional Chinese Medicine knowledge graph construction method. Data are collected using user-input keywords, structured using BERT-CRF for named entity recognition and Bootstrapping for relation extraction, and merged into an existing knowledge graph to support dynamic construction and user-friendly search.

problem_addressed: Existing TCM knowledge graphs are generally constructed once from currently available data and therefore cannot continuously incorporate multi-source information in response to users' search needs. The paper aims to construct a TCM knowledge graph that grows dynamically when a user's query is not covered by the existing graph.

methodology.description: The system is a query-triggered pipeline. For each keyword in a user search, it collects related public data from several fixed websites and keeps sentences satisfying downstream processing requirements. BERT-CRF converts each sentence into BIO-labelled entity spans for six TCM-specific entity types: color, form, smell, taste, cause, and symptom. A Bootstrapping procedure begins with expert-defined semantic patterns and seed entity pairs, removes entities, participles, and stop words to identify relation-trigger candidates, expands the semantic-pattern and trigger-word sets, and uses expert review to finalize trigger words. It extracts cause–symptom triples when a finalized trigger occurs between an entity pair. The newly constructed graph is merged with the existing graph by replacing an entity in the new graph with an existing entity when they are considered the same; otherwise the entity is added, followed by adding new relations and facts. The updated graph is then shown to the user. No separate mechanism is reported for coreference resolution, general entity linking, entity typing beyond the six predefined types, ontology discovery, or graph validation beyond the merge/refinement rule.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The method uses an expert-defined extraction schema rather than discovering an ontology. Six entity types are defined—color, form, smell, taste, cause, and symptom—with 13 BIO labels. Relations are constrained to the disease-symptoms-caused-by-causes relation between cause and symptom entities; color, form, smell, and taste types are treated as already carrying relational information.

input_output.input_type: Public Traditional Chinese Medicine textual data collected from several fixed websites in response to user search keywords.
input_output.input_granularity: Sentence-level processing after collecting textual data; the evaluation uses data associated with searches for individual medicines.
input_output.output_representation: Typed entity nodes and cause–symptom relation triples, merged into a dynamically updated TCM knowledge graph represented as G = {E, R, F}, where facts are triples (head, relation, tail).

models_and_tools: Automatic data collection and graph-merging algorithms
datasets: TCM dataset assembled from public data collected from several fixed websites; the paper does not provide a formal dataset name or source list.
Evaluation collection consisting of ten randomly selected Traditional Chinese medicines searched sequentially, including Erdong Gao.

metrics: Cumulative number of entities by type after each retrieval
Cumulative number of relations after each retrieval
Qualitative observation of graph growth with user retrievals
evaluation.setting: The authors build the graph from scratch, randomly select ten TCM medicines, search them in sequence, and count cumulative entities and relations as retrievals increase. The implementation uses Python 3.8 on 64-bit Windows 10 with 32 GB RAM and an Intel i7-4790K CPU. No extraction-accuracy test set, train/test split, or baseline comparison is reported.

value: Table 3 reports cumulative entity totals of 0, 12, 17, 29, 37, 48, 62, 76, 85, 94, and 107 after 0 through 10 retrievals, respectively.
After 10 retrievals, the entity counts are 12 color, 11 form, 5 smell, 11 taste, 20 cause, and 48 symptom entities, totaling 107.
The relation plot shows that the cumulative number of relations increases as retrievals increase; the paper concludes that the graph grows dynamically with user retrieval behavior.
The paper reports that the resulting triples are merged into the pre-existing graph to provide more comprehensive retrieval service.

value: Author-stated strength: the method is triggered by user search keywords and can integrate public multi-source data incrementally instead of relying only on a one-time graph construction.
Author-stated strength: BERT-CRF is used for entity extraction and Bootstrapping for relation extraction, followed by merging structured data into an existing graph.
Review-level inference: the explicit six-type schema and cause–symptom relation restrict the extraction space, which may simplify implementation in the targeted TCM setting.
Review-level inference: the evaluation directly tests the intended dynamic-growth behavior by tracking graph contents across successive retrievals.
